paragraphs: The passage from the state of nature to the civil state produces a very remarkable change in man. It substitutes justice for instinct in his conduct and gives his actions the morality they previously lacked. Only then, when the voice of duty takes the place of physical impulse, and right takes the place of appetite, does _man_, who until now had considered only himself, find that he is forced to act on different principles and to consult his reason before listening to his inclinations. In this state he deprives himself of some advantages he had from nature, but he gains others so great in return. His faculties are so stimulated and developed, his ideas so broadened, his feelings so ennobled, and his whole soul so uplifted, that, if the abuses of this new condition did not often degrade him below the one he left, he would be bound to bless continually the happy moment that took him from it forever, and that made him, instead of a stupid and unimaginative animal, an intelligent being and a man.

Let us draw up the whole account in terms that are easy to compare. What man loses by the social contract is his natural liberty and an unlimited right to everything he tries to get and succeeds in getting; what he gains is civil liberty and ownership of everything he possesses. To avoid mistakes in weighing one against the other, we must clearly distinguish natural liberty, which is bounded only by the strength of the individual, from civil liberty, which is limited by the general will. We must also distinguish possession, which is merely the effect of force or the right of the first occupier, from property, which can be founded only on a positive title.

On top of all this, we might add to what man acquires in the civil state moral liberty, which alone makes him truly master of himself; for the mere impulse of appetite is slavery, while obedience to a law that we prescribe to ourselves is liberty. But I have already said too much on this subject, and the philosophical meaning of the word liberty does not concern us here.
